root_cause.text: Missing bounds check in __rlookup_amd_iommu() for devid against pci_seg->last_bdf before indexing into the rlookup_table array, leading to an out-of-bounds read when a PCI device's BDF is not covered by the IVRS.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "__rlookup_amd_iommu() indexes rlookup_table[devid] with no bounds check of its own, so for a PCI device whose BDF is not described by the IVRS, the lookup reads past the end of the allocation before the caller's bounds check can run." The patch adds the condition "if (devid > pci_seg->last_bdf) return NULL;" to prevent the out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: Declaration of the pointer used to access the rlookup_table; without bounds check, the indexed access is unsafe.
Loop that iterates over PCI segments; provides the pci_seg pointer used in the subsequent vulnerable index operation.
Condition to match the PCI segment; passes control to the vulnerable return statement without checking devid bounds.
Directly indexes into rlookup_table using devid without verifying devid is within bounds, causing out-of-bounds read when devid exceeds the table size.
Fallback return after the loop; if the loop completes without matching segment, returns NULL, but the vulnerable return may already have been executed.
